items.title: CVE-2026-68820: Windows WinSock (afd.sys) Zero-Day Actively Exploited, Added to CISA KEV
items.summary: A use-after-free vulnerability in the Windows Ancillary Function Driver for WinSock (afd.sys) is being actively exploited in the wild to elevate privileges to SYSTEM. Patched in Microsoft's August 2026 Patch Tuesday alongside 420 other CVEs.
items.why: Confirmed in-the-wild exploitation and already listed in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue. Historical afd.sys targeting patterns suggest potential nation-state actor involvement. Affects all supported Windows versions — patch immediately.
items.source: SecurityWeek / Microsoft / CrowdStrike Patch Tuesday Analysis

items.title: CVE-2026-62878: Windows DNS Server Wormable RCE (CVSS 9.8) — Unauthenticated Stack Overflow
items.summary: An unauthenticated stack-based buffer overflow in the Windows DNS Server enables remote code execution from the network with no credentials required. CVSS 9.8 and classified as potentially wormable due to its network-reachable attack vector.
items.why: Wormable CVSS 9.8 RCE on DNS servers is as dangerous as it gets for network infrastructure. A successful exploit could allow an attacker to move laterally across an entire enterprise by chaining DNS server compromise. Prioritize patching all Windows DNS Server deployments.
items.source: Zero Day Initiative / Microsoft August 2026 Patch Tuesday

items.title: Supply Chain Attack via Trojanized Trivy Scanner Nets 153GB: AWS, Samsung, Cisco Secrets Stolen
items.summary: Attackers compromised the popular open-source Trivy vulnerability scanner and weaponized it with infostealer malware. The campaign exfiltrated 153GB of data including Git credentials, CI/CD pipeline secrets, cryptowallets, and cloud API keys from organizations including AWS, Samsung, and Cisco.
items.why: A trusted security tool turned into an attack vector is a high-impact supply chain scenario. CI/CD credential theft gives attackers keys to downstream software pipelines. Any organization running Trivy in automated pipelines should immediately audit secrets, rotate credentials, and verify binary integrity.

items.title: Iranian APT 'Screening Serpens' Escalates Espionage Operations Across Five Countries
items.summary: Palo Alto Unit 42 is tracking the Iranian-nexus group Screening Serpens, which has significantly increased operations since a regional conflict beginning in February 2026. The group deploys two previously undocumented RAT variants against government and critical-sector targets in at least five countries.
items.why: State-sponsored escalation tied to active geopolitical conflict signals a broadening threat surface. Novel custom RAT families indicate investment in detection evasion. Organizations in the Middle East, Europe, and allied government sectors should raise alert levels for Iranian TTPs.

items.title: CrowdStrike 2026 Global Threat Report: AI-Enabled Adversaries Up 89%, eCrime Breakout Time Drops to 29 Minutes
items.summary: CrowdStrike's 2026 Global Threat Report documents an 89% surge in AI-accelerated eCrime activity, with average adversary breakout time (initial access to lateral movement) now just 29 minutes. Mandiant's M-Trends 2026 corroborates: exploits remain the #1 initial access vector for the sixth consecutive year.
items.why: Sub-30-minute breakout times eliminate any margin for human-speed detection and response. The democratization of AI offensive tooling is lowering the barrier for sophisticated attacks across the eCrime ecosystem. Defenders must shift to automated, pre-emptive controls and assume breach posture as the default.
items.source: CrowdStrike 2026 Global Threat Report / Mandiant M-Trends 2026
